bottlenecks.description: Domain shift across imaging sites and scanners causes significant performance degradation in deployed models. Non-biological variations in hardware, acquisition protocols, and patient populations lead to models failing on external validation data.
bottlenecks.evidence: Dalmaz et al. (2024) 'Improving Multi-Center Generalizability of GAN-Based Fat Suppression using Federated Learning'; Wei et al. (2019) domain shift in multi-site MRI; FedDAPL (2025) 'Toward Client-Private Generalization in Federated Learning'

bottlenecks.description: GPU memory constraints for whole slide image (WSI) processing in computational pathology. A single WSI at 40x magnification can be 100,000 x 100,000 pixels (~2GB compressed, ~30GB uncompressed), making end-to-end training on a single GPU infeasible without tiling strategies that sacrifice spatial context.
bottlenecks.evidence: FBTA paper (CVPR 2026) 'Enabling Single-GPU End-to-End Gigapixel WSI Classification'; arccompute.io GPU infrastructure analysis; Lu et al. (2021) 'Federated learning for computational pathology on gigapixel whole slide images'

bottlenecks.description: Annotation scarcity and cost. Pixel-level manual annotation by expert radiologists and pathologists is expensive and time-consuming, leading to small, heavily curated datasets that limit model generalization.
bottlenecks.evidence: Campanella et al. (2019) 'Clinical-grade computational pathology using weakly supervised deep learning on whole slide images' Nature Medicine; Isensee et al. (2021) nnU-Net Nature Methods

bottlenecks.description: Inference latency requirements in acute care settings. AI triage for stroke, pulmonary embolism, and chest X-ray interpretation requires results within seconds to minutes, creating real-time constraints that cloud offloading cannot reliably guarantee.
bottlenecks.evidence: arccompute.io 'GPU Infrastructure for Medical Imaging AI' - clinical SLA requirements; Efficient Deep Learning for Medical Imaging (2025) arXiv:2602.00910

bottlenecks.description: Data privacy regulations (HIPAA, GDPR) hinder data consolidation for training, creating data silos that limit model performance and generalizability.
bottlenecks.evidence: Kaissis et al. (2024) 'Reconciling privacy and accuracy in AI for medical imaging' Nature Machine Intelligence; Scientific Reports (2024) 'The potential of federated learning for self-configuring medical object detection'

bottlenecks.description: Diffusion models for 3D medical image synthesis require hundreds of sequential U-Net evaluations per sample, demanding hundreds of GPU-hours even for modest datasets.
bottlenecks.evidence: Performance Analysis of 3D Generative Diffusion Models (2025) arXiv:2606.19365 - Med-DDPM analysis

bottlenecks.description: Quadratic scaling of self-attention in transformer architectures limits applicability to gigapixel histopathology slides and high-resolution 3D volumetric scans.
bottlenecks.evidence: Efficient Deep Learning for Medical Imaging (2025) arXiv:2602.00910 - State Space Models (Mamba) as alternative

np_hard_problems.problem: Optimal patch selection and tiling strategy for whole slide image analysis under memory constraints
np_hard_problems.complexity: NP-hard (reduces to maximum coverage problem with spatial constraints)
current_approaches: Two-stage patch-to-bag pipelines with frozen feature extractors
Multiple Instance Learning (MIL) with attention-based pooling
Pseudo-bag construction via Instance Sampling without Replacement (ISR) with KMeans clustering
gaps: Frozen feature extractors create semantic gap with downstream classification objective
End-to-end backpropagation through tens of thousands of patches exceeds single-GPU memory
Tiling sacrifices spatial context critical for diagnosis

np_hard_problems.problem: Multi-objectivity optimization for segmentation architecture search (accuracy vs. computational cost vs. memory footprint)
current_approaches: nnU-Net self-configuring framework with rule-based architecture selection
Auto3DSeg with SegResNet, DiNTS, SwinUNETR architectures
Neural architecture search (NAS) with hardware-aware constraints
gaps: Search space grows exponentially with number of objectives
Hardware-specific optima do not transfer across GPU generations
No guarantee of Pareto optimality in practice

np_hard_problems.problem: Feature selection and dimensionality reduction for radiomics-based classification
gaps: High-dimensional feature spaces (thousands of radiomic features) with small sample sizes

np_hard_problems.problem: Optimal client selection and aggregation strategy for federated learning with non-IID data distributions
current_approaches: Domain-adversarial neural networks (DANN) with proximal regularization (FedDAPL)
gaps: Communication rounds scale with number of clients

sota_approaches.name: nnU-Net
sota_approaches.description: Self-configuring framework for U-Net-based medical image segmentation that automatically adapts preprocessing, architecture, training, and postprocessing to any dataset without manual intervention. Achieves state-of-the-art on 23 public datasets across multiple modalities.
sota_approaches.citation: Isensee et al. (2021) 'nnU-Net: a self-configuring method for deep learning-based biomedical image segmentation' Nature Methods 18:203-211. doi:10.1038/s41592-020-01008-z

sota_approaches.name: MONAI (Medical Open Network for AI)
sota_approaches.description: PyTorch-based open-source framework for deep learning in healthcare imaging with domain-specific transforms, validated 3D architectures (UNETR, SwinUNETR, VISTA-3D), and reproducible clinical deployment pipelines.
sota_approaches.citation: Cardoso et al. (2022) 'MONAI: An open-source framework for deep learning in healthcare' arXiv:2204.12318. https://github.com/Project-MONAI/MONAI

sota_approaches.name: Curia
sota_approaches.description: Multi-modal foundation model for radiology trained on 200+ million CT and MRI images (130TB, 150K exams) using DINOv2 self-supervised learning. Meets or surpasses radiologist performance on 19-task external validation benchmark.
sota_approaches.citation: Dancette et al. (2025) 'Curia: A Multi-Modal Foundation Model for Radiology' arXiv:2509.06830

sota_approaches.name: nnFoundation
sota_approaches.description: 3D foundation models for radiology trained on 2.1 million CT, MRI, and PET volumes from 125 datasets. Convolutional and transformer variants evaluated on 108 tasks including segmentation, detection, classification, and report generation.
sota_approaches.citation: Human Radiome Project (2025) 'nnFoundation: 3D Foundation Models for Radiology' arXiv:2609.26924

sota_approaches.name: TITAN
sota_approaches.description: Multimodal whole-slide foundation model for pathology pretrained on 335,645 WSIs with vision-language alignment using pathology reports and synthetic captions. Enables zero-shot classification, rare cancer retrieval, and pathology report generation.
sota_approaches.citation: Ding et al. (2024) 'Multimodal Whole Slide Foundation Model for Pathology' arXiv:2411.19666

sota_approaches.name: PanDerm
sota_approaches.description: Multimodal dermatology foundation model pretrained on 2+ million skin disease images from 11 clinical institutions across 4 imaging modalities. Outperforms clinicians by 10.2% in early-stage melanoma detection.
sota_approaches.citation: Nature Medicine (2025) 'A multimodal vision foundation model for clinical dermatology' doi:10.1038/s41591-025-03747-y

sota_approaches.name: Federated Learning with Differential Privacy
sota_approaches.description: Privacy-preserving collaborative training across institutions without data sharing. HistoFL framework for computational pathology on gigapixel WSIs with weakly-supervised attention MIL and differential privacy.
sota_approaches.citation: Lu et al. (2021) 'Federated learning for computational pathology on gigapixel whole slide images' Medical Image Analysis. https://github.com/mahmoodlab/HistoFL

failure_modes.mode: Domain shift and poor generalization to external sites
failure_modes.mitigation: Federated learning with domain generalization (FedDAPL), multi-site validation, domain adaptation techniques, and continuous monitoring of model performance across sites
Self-supervised pretraining on large unlabeled datasets, data augmentation, transfer learning from foundation models, and few-shot learning approaches

failure_modes.mode: Hallucination in generative models for image synthesis
failure_modes.mitigation: Physics-informed models, multi-site validation, uncertainty quantification, and human-in-the-loop verification

failure_modes.mode: Dataset bias and health equity disparities
failure_modes.mitigation: Diffusion-based synthetic data generation for underrepresented groups, fairness-aware machine learning, and diverse multi-site training cohorts

failure_modes.mode: Adversarial attacks and model inversion privacy risks
failure_modes.mitigation: Differential privacy, secure aggregation, federated learning, and robust model hardening techniques

failure_modes.mode: Alert fatigue from high false-positive rates
failure_modes.mitigation: Threshold optimization, uncertainty-aware prediction, and human-AI collaborative decision-making frameworks

hardware_requirements.minimum: Single GPU with 24GB VRAM (e.g., RTX 3090) for 2D image analysis and lightweight models; 80GB VRAM (A100) for production WSI inference at 40x magnification
hardware_requirements.recommended: Multi-GPU nodes with NVIDIA H100 (80GB HBM3) or H200 (141GB HBM3e) for training; Blackwell B200 (192GB HBM3e) for large-scale foundation model training and WSI analysis without tiling; NVLink/NVSwitch interconnects for multi-GPU scaling

scalability_limits.threshold: Single WSI at 40x magnification: ~100,000 x 100,000 pixels (~2GB compressed, ~30GB uncompressed); requires 80GB+ VRAM for production inference without tiling
3D medical diffusion models require hundreds of GPU-hours even for modest datasets; single sample requires hundreds of sequential U-Net evaluations
Communication rounds scale with number of clients; non-IID data requires more rounds for convergence; differential privacy adds noise that slows convergence
Quadratic scaling O(n²) with image resolution limits application to gigapixel WSIs and high-resolution 3D volumes; State Space Models (Mamba) offer linear scaling alternative
3D radiology foundation models require millions of volumes (nnFoundation: 2.1M volumes from 125 datasets); pathology foundation models require 300K+ WSIs (TITAN: 335,645 WSIs)
Acute care AI triage requires <5 minutes for stroke CT, <10 minutes for PE detection, <2 minutes for chest X-ray preliminary read; cloud offloading cannot reliably guarantee these SLAs

regulations: FDA 510(k) Premarket Notification - 97% of AI/ML medical devices cleared via this pathway; 168 ML-enabled devices approved in 2024 alone
FDA De Novo Pathway - for novel devices without predicate; 9 devices (5.4%) in 2024
EU MDR 2017/745 - Medical Device Regulation; most AI diagnostic software classified as Class IIa or higher requiring Notified Body review
EU AI Act 2024/1689 - AI-enabled medical devices automatically classified as high-risk AI; full obligations apply from August 2028 for medical devices
HIPAA - Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act for patient data protection in the US
GDPR - General Data Protection Regulation for health data in the EU
ISO 13485 - Quality management systems for medical devices
IEC 62304 - Medical device software lifecycle processes
challenges: Dual regulatory burden in EU: MDR + AI Act compliance required simultaneously
Predetermined Change Control Plans (PCCP) needed for adaptive AI models but not yet standardized
Notified Body shortage in EU causing 12-24 month review timelines
Post-market surveillance and real-world performance monitoring requirements
Data governance: training data must be relevant, representative, free of errors, and complete
Algorithmic transparency and human oversight requirements
Cybersecurity requirements for connected AI medical devices
Equity and bias assessment across demographic groups and skin tones

cost_tradeoffs.approach: Cloud-based inference (e.g., GPT-4 for radiology report analysis)
cost_tradeoffs.cost: $134 per report (13±4 seconds); ongoing operational expense
cost_tradeoffs.benefit: No hardware investment; scalable compute on demand

cost_tradeoffs.cost: $10,000-$30,000 per GPU; $100K+ for multi-GPU node; power and cooling
cost_tradeoffs.benefit: Low latency for real-time triage; data sovereignty; no per-inference cost

cost_tradeoffs.cost: Higher communication overhead; complex infrastructure; slower convergence
cost_tradeoffs.benefit: Privacy preservation; multi-site collaboration without data sharing; regulatory compliance

cost_tradeoffs.approach: Foundation model fine-tuning vs. task-specific training
cost_tradeoffs.cost: Pretraining requires millions of images and thousands of GPU-hours; fine-tuning is cheaper
cost_tradeoffs.benefit: Superior generalization; few-shot learning capability; reduced annotation requirements

cost_tradeoffs.cost: Privacy-accuracy tradeoff; noise injection degrades model performance
cost_tradeoffs.benefit: Mathematical privacy guarantees; regulatory compliance; protection against model inversion attacks
4x memory reduction; 2-4x speedup; enables deployment on edge devices and mobile NPUs
